Maya S: Quick note — I ran a small set of narrowbench cases on the new 70B-L2 drop. results looked weird for awq-int8 on reasoning tasks.
Jason R: can you paste the exact config you used? batch sizes / seq len?
Maya S: sure — single-GPU, seq=1024, batch=4, awq-int8, fallback policy = none. here is the smoke config:
```yaml
model: 70b-l2
quant: awq-int8
seq_len: 1024
batch: 4
routing: hosted-primary,dedicated-fallback
fallback_policy:
  threshold: 0.82
  mode: degrade-to-fp8
```
Liam K: interesting — we usually set threshold at 0.88 for reasoning. 0.82 will trigger a lot of fallbacks.
Maya S: yeah this was intentional for stress testing. observed ~6.2% exact-match drop vs fp8 on arithmetic suite, but perplexity similar.
Priya N: can we add the narrowbench diff and a tiny eval set? throw in a few model outputs for regression triage.
Maya S: attached sample outputs below (shortened):
```
Q: 123 + 456 = ?
FP8: 579
AWQ-INT8: 580 (off-by-one across odd examples)
``` 
Emily T: hmm off-by-one bias — could be quantization rounding on attention or matmul accum. Did you try gptq and int8-gptq?
Maya S: ran GPTQ-INT8 baseline too — delta was +1.1% vs fp8 (better than awq here). AWQ seems to mis-handle a numeric drift.
quant-bot: [Auto eval] uploaded: /artifacts/1804567890/narrowbench/v1 — reports/summary.json
Jason R: proposal: we adopt a "handover corridor" rule for canaries — allow aggressive int8 on hosted read-only routes but force a tighter quality corridor for dedicated/private. corridor = {max_delta:0.5%, blacklist: arithmetic-suite}
Priya N: agree on corridor idea. also add runtime heuristics: if error spike > X for 5m, instant rollback to fp8 on that route.
Liam K: operationally, that means two policies: rollout_policy.hosted and rollout_policy.dedicated. hosted can have permissive quant profiles + cache warming; dedicated/private default to conservative.
Maya S: sketch of rollout YAML I propose:
```yaml
rollout:
  hosted:
    allowed_quants: [fp8, gptq-int8, awq-int8]
    quality_corridor: 1.2
    auto_warm_kv: true
  dedicated:
    allowed_quants: [fp8, gptq-int8]
    quality_corridor: 0.5
    circuit_breaker: {error_rate:0.03, window:300}
  private:
    allowed_quants: [fp8]
    quality_corridor: 0.2
```
Emily T: sounds good. add a metric for "semantic-sanity" (BLEU/ROUGE-ish surrogate + task-specific golden checks) not just perplexity.
Jason R: Can we run a short A/B on hosted with AWQ areal and GPTQ vs FP8 for the arithmetic and code-gen small sets? 1% bucket each, 24h.
Maya S: I can spin up the job today. will include telemetry hooks: token-level error tags and trace ids.
Priya N: also include memory footprint + p50/p95 latency. we need unit economics to justify awq on hosted.
Maya S: noted. starting job, will post artifacts when done. @quant-bot schedule 24h ab_test job: 70b-l2 {awq-int8,gptq-int8,fp8} ratio=1:1:1 seq=512 batch=8
quant-bot: A/B job queued: job_id=bakeoff-1804567890-1 queued by Maya S
Jason R: sweet. if we see systematic regression, we'll push corridor tightening and auto-fallback on that route. :thumbsup:
